title: Demo Roadmap: Foundations → Applications
subject: Demo
description: A throwaway three-node fixture for building and proving the graph framework.

nodes.title: Foundations
nodes.summary: Foundations introduces the core building blocks every later topic depends on: the basic vocabulary, the simplest rules, and the mental models you will reuse everywhere. We start from first principles, define each term precisely, and show small worked examples so the ideas feel concrete rather than abstract. By the end you can name the fundamental pieces, explain how they fit together, and recognise them when they reappear in more advanced settings. This node is the root of the roadmap and has no prerequisites, so it is always available to begin.

resources.title: A Gentle Introduction to the Basics

nodes.title: Core Concepts
nodes.summary: Core Concepts builds directly on the foundations, combining the basic pieces into the central ideas that make the subject useful. Here we move from isolated definitions to relationships: how the building blocks interact, which patterns recur, and why certain rules hold. We work through intermediate examples that require holding two or three ideas in mind at once, and we highlight the common mistakes learners make at this stage. Mastering this node unlocks the applications topic, because real applications assume a fluent command of these concepts rather than just the raw fundamentals.

nodes.title: Applications
nodes.summary: Applications is where the roadmap pays off: we take the foundations and core concepts and apply them to realistic problems end to end. Each example begins with a messy, real-world prompt and walks through choosing the right tools, justifying each step, and checking the result for sense. Because this node sits at the end of the dependency chain, it stays locked until the core concepts are mastered, mirroring how real expertise compounds. By the end you can tackle unfamiliar problems independently, transfer the techniques to new domains, and explain your reasoning clearly to others.
